newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti looking for PC partners--Caio.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti looking for PC partners--Caio.

text.p: Italy's struggling information technology group Olivetti said on Thursday its future prospects lay in the area of telecommunications and services, while it was looking for a partner for its loss-making personal computer company.
This was outlined in a testimony given by the group's chief executive Francesco Caio at the upper house Senate industrial commission this morning.
"The future of Olivetti is positioned between the business of systems and services and telecommunications. For the other businesses we must find partnerships or alliances," Caio said.

"We are committed to finding alliances in personal computers. We are looking for partners who recognise the opportunity to develop and make investments in these sectors, to assure a future for the activities that Olivetti has built up," he said.
"Olivetti must make choices to maximise its own resources in sectors in which it has the possibility of showing leadership," Caio added.
Referring to Olivetti's Lexikon office equipment business he said, "The company is profitable but it is exposed to risks which need action if we want to guarantee its development".
"Lexikon has sales of around two trillion lire and is in a traditionally strong position, but which has to take into account increasingly fierce competition.
